newsitem.title: USA: Clinton-Yeltsin summit expected in Helsinki.
newsitem.headline: Clinton-Yeltsin summit expected in Helsinki.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin are expected to hold a summit meeting in March in Helsinki, U.S. officials said on Friday.

The officials said the site and date were agreed upon during meetings between Vice President Al Gore and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who were to announce the details later. They were scheduled to hold a news conference at 11:30 a.m. EST (1630 GMT)
The summit date was expected to be in the latter part of March.

It is Yeltsin's turn to visit the United States, since Clinton went to Moscow for the last summit in April. But U.S. officials were receptive to Russian suggestions the summit be moved to a third country closer to Russia because of Yeltsin's slow recovery from heart bypass surgery and pneumonia.
Finnish diplomatic officials said Finland was happy to welcome the two leaders, having played host to a summit in 1990 between then-President George Bush and then-Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev.
